expectations.text: Flags the getOrder handler in OrdersController as missing an ownership check, citing it by file (src/orders/orders.controller.ts) and function name (getOrder)
expectations.evidence: '[high] IDOR — getOrder has no ownership check — src/orders/orders.controller.ts:8-10' — cites both file and function.

expectations.text: Does not flag cancelOrder as vulnerable, since it already fetches the order and checks order.userId !== user.id before mutating it — restraint / false-positive check
expectations.evidence: Explicit 'IDOR check (Step 3)' section marks cancelOrder **safe** and calls it the correct template. No false positive.

expectations.text: Assigns high severity to the getOrder finding

Explains the exploitable scenario: any authenticated user can fetch another user's order by supplying or guessing an arbitrary orderId, since getOrder returns whatever findUnique returns with no check against the caller
expectations.evidence: 'Any authenticated user who knows or guesses an orderId (sequential IDs, leaked from another response, enumerated) can read another customer's order.'

expectations.text: The suggested fix for getOrder matches the ownership-check shape used in cancelOrder: fetch the order, then reject when the order is missing or order.userId !== user.id (e.g. throwing ForbiddenException) before returning it
expectations.evidence: Proposed fix fetches then throws ForbiddenException when !order || order.userId !== user.id — the same shape as cancelOrder, explicitly 'mirror the check already present in cancelOrder'.

expectations.text: Uses the skill's report structure: a numbered, severity-tagged finding referencing the file, distinct from an unstructured paragraph
expectations.evidence: Numbered severity-tagged findings under a report header with per-section structure.
